deck: BUY A CASH-FLOWING SMALL BUSINESS AT 2.5-4.5X EARNINGS INSTEAD OF STARTING ONE
SOURCE, SCREEN, LOI, DILIGENCE, SBA 7(A) FINANCE, AND OPERATE THE FIRST 100 DAYS
site_ui.lead: Professors, brokers, attorneys, and searchers make the case that buying a cash-flowing small business at a half to a third of private equity multiples, financed with SBA 7(a) debt and a seller note, beats starting one from scratch.
site_ui.summary: All 12 chapters synthesize 192 verbatim YouTube practitioner testimonies on entrepreneurship through acquisition, from deal sourcing and SBA lending through LOI drafting, quality of earnings, closing mechanics, and post-acquisition integration. Every claim, metric, pro-tip, and operator gate carries timestamped inline attribution to the source video.

flow: Work brokers, trade-show lists, and belly-to-belly direct outreach in one geography, targeting $1-5M revenue businesses and reviewing every listing to build reps.
Price at about 2.5-4.5x earnings, kill razor-thin-margin labor- or capital-intensive targets, and flag any client above 10% of sales or a top-five list routed through one referrer.
Open low near 2.5x and concede a quarter or half turn, refuse deposits and breakage fees on small deals, and strike working capital pegs from Main Street asset deals.
Run legal, then financial, then operational review over about 60 days with a QoE, 36 months of reconciled bank statements, and time cards pulled by hand; kill any target with two sets of books.
Fund with SBA 7(a) debt up to $5M for up to 90% of price with a personal guarantee, plus a seller note or earnout and $100-150K of working capital.
Freeze personnel changes for six months, keep your salary low, name an owner for every P&L line, book the top 20 customers, and change processes incrementally in months 3-7.
